summary: This bill amends the Immigration and Nationality Act to make any alien convicted of (or admitting to) animal cruelty or fighting under federal law (18 U.S.C. 48 or 49) or equivalent state, tribal, or local law both inadmissible and deportable.

scores.thoughts: The bill contains no provisions related to federal spending, appropriations, or budget allocations. It solely amends immigration law regarding admissibility and deportability.
No provisions address taxes, tax rates, deductions, or revenue collection.
The bill does not engage with healthcare policy, coverage, or regulation in any way.
No references to firearms, gun regulations, or Second Amendment issues.

The bill directly amends the Immigration and Nationality Act (sections 212 and 237) to add convictions for animal cruelty or animal fighting (under federal, state, tribal, or local law) as grounds for inadmissibility and deportability. This expands enforcement mechanisms and removal criteria for noncitizens, clearly advancing immigration restriction and border enforcement priorities.
No provisions relate to reproductive rights or abortion access.
The bill has no connection to military or defense spending or policy.
No environmental regulations, protections, or climate-related measures are addressed.
The legislation does not affect welfare programs, entitlements, or social safety net policies.
No provisions involve schools, education funding, or school choice.
The bill does not address drug enforcement, decriminalization, or controlled substances.

While the bill references criminal convictions for animal cruelty as a trigger for immigration consequences, it does not alter sentencing, policing, rehabilitation, or criminal justice procedures themselves. Any connection is incidental and secondary to its immigration focus.
No trade, tariffs, or globalization provisions are present.
The bill has no fiscal or debt-related implications.
No provisions address LGBTQ+ legal protections or rights.
The bill does not involve foreign aid or international assistance.
No election integrity, voting access, or electoral reform measures are included.
